_doc: THE EXIT CONDITION FOR THE WORKFLOW OVERHAUL. Operator directive 2026-09-03: 'we need to finish the workflow overhaul before the roadmap review, INCLUDING VERIFYING THE THINGS THAT HAVE SHIPPED.' ⚠️ THAT SHARPENS THE EARLIER SEQUENCING AND MAKES THIS THE CRITICAL PATH: the remaining PR queue is the SMALL half. The big half is 26 rows sitting at `landed_unproven` -- merged, with their effect NEVER OBSERVED on the fleet. `done` means MERGED AND OBSERVED; `landed_unproven` means the code is in and nobody has seen it work. Collapsing those two is the failure this repo has paid for repeatedly, and phase 2 does not start until this list is worked.
population: 26 rows at landed_unproven in docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, measured 2026-09-03T11:48Z over all 97 items. Counted, not estimated.
why_this_is_not_just_a_checklist_sweep: Verification is a DIFFERENT KIND OF WORK from building, and some of it CANNOT be done by the session that built the thing. A session that knows about a mechanism cannot be the cold reader that proves the mechanism reaches a session that does not. That is why several of these have sat unproven for days: they were never blocked on effort, they were blocked on nobody being in a position to observe them.

A_COLD_SESSION.what_it_needs: A session NOT pointed at the mechanism by its prompt, observed using it. ⚠️ THE MANAGER CANNOT PRODUCE THIS BY ASKING FOR IT -- asking contaminates the observation, which is exactly what OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION and OI-20260901-CYCLE-PRIORITY-IS-RENDERED both say in their own clears_when. The only honest route is to spawn ordinary work and READ WHAT THE SESSION DID unprompted.
A_COLD_SESSION.note: This class also covers the Phases A-D `waiting` lifecycle in the work store -- their code shipped and the cold read is what is missing.

B_LIVE_FLEET_READ.what_it_needs: A diag read of real runtime behaviour on the live VM. Available to any session with the diag path; bounded and cheap per row. ⚠️ A PASSING TEST IS NOT THIS.
B_LIVE_FLEET_READ.note: SIX OF THESE ARE ONE SUBSYSTEM -- the ping/comms chain (MI-01, MI-02, MI-16, MI-17, MI-80, MI-83). They should be verified TOGETHER by one session in one pass, not six times. ⚠️ AND ONE IS ALREADY PART-CLEARED: the per-merge ping was CONFIRMED DELIVERED by the operator today (#10917), which is the first real evidence in that whole chain -- start there rather than from zero.

C_EXERCISED_BY_USE.what_it_needs: The mechanism being USED under real conditions, then read back. Several were exercised TODAY and the evidence already exists -- these are the cheapest and should go first.
C_EXERCISED_BY_USE.note: ⚠️ TODAY'S QUEUE JAM WAS THE EXERCISE for MI-20 / MI-35 / MI-94: 26 merges to main, 19 (73%) touching a shared register, #10918 conflicted three times, the merge driver armed in ZERO clones, and the driver proven CLIENT-SIDE ONLY -- it removes the hand-resolution and never the GitHub-side dirty state. That is real evidence and it is already measured; these rows can be closed or sharpened on it TODAY. ⚠️ MI-98 IS THE OPPOSITE CASE and must NOT be closed: measured 11:25Z, its fix is FORWARD-LOOKING ONLY and the 12 already-open automation PRs still fail R11. ⚠️ MI-70 needs a DELIBERATE ACT -- killing a session mid-work -- and nobody has done it.

order: 1. CLASS C FIRST, and specifically the rows today already exercised (MI-20, MI-35, MI-94, MI-89, MI-93, MI-100). The evidence exists; this is reading and recording, not new work, and it is the fastest reduction of the 26.

2. THE PING CHAIN as ONE unit (MI-01, MI-02, MI-16, MI-17, MI-80, MI-83) -- six rows, one subsystem, one session, one pass. Start from the per-merge ping the operator confirmed today rather than from zero.
3. THE REMAINING CLASS B LIVE READS (MI-09, MI-10, MI-27, MI-36, MI-90) -- independent, bounded, parallelisable.
4. MI-70 -- the deliberate session kill. Its own row says prove it by ACTUALLY killing a session mid-work; a simulation is not the proof.

5. CLASS A COLD-SESSION LAST, because it is the one class the manager cannot manufacture. It clears as a SIDE EFFECT of ordinary work being spawned, so it should ride whatever comes next rather than blocking the gate.
the_honest_risk: ⚠️ CLASS A MAY NOT CLEAR BEFORE THE ROADMAP REVIEW, AND PRETENDING OTHERWISE WOULD BE THE FAILURE THIS WHOLE PLAN EXISTS TO PREVENT. Six rows need an UNCONTAMINATED cold observation, and the manager cannot produce one on demand without destroying it. If the operator wants phase 2 to start, the honest options are: (a) accept Class A as explicitly OUTSTANDING with a named carrier, or (b) hold phase 2 until ordinary work happens to clear them. What must NOT happen is Class A being marked verified because a session was told to go look -- that is the contaminated observation those rows' own clears_when text forbids by name.
what_done_means: A row leaves `landed_unproven` ONLY on an OBSERVATION of the mechanism working on the fleet, recorded in the row. Not a passing test. Not a merged diff. Not 'the code is obviously correct'. And a row whose verification FAILS is a better outcome than one quietly marked done -- MI-98 is today's example: verifying it found the fix is forward-only, which is a finding worth more than the merge.
